title: Developer caches & build artifacts
_comment: Regenerable caches created by developer tools. method: rm = delete permanently, rmforce = chmod +w then delete (for read-only caches like Go modules & Cargo sources). Paths may use ~ and * globs, and may start with @cache/, @temp/ or @boot-temp/ for this user's own C, T and X under /private/var/folders (docs/DESIGN.md#user-folder). default:true = pre-selected. Rule of thumb for default: true means 'costs a rebuild or a small re-download'; false means 'costs a large re-download, or the data may not regenerate on its own' — and anything that removes installed software is false. A 'kind' works out its offer in the script and takes its globs from 'images' or 'candidates', never 'paths', so a cdm too old to know the kind offers nothing: android-images (system images no AVD boots), android-idle-images (images only AVDs idle for 'idleDays' boot, one row each), older-versions (each glob is one family of versions; all but the newest), rust-toolchains (toolchains other than the default and stable, removed with 'rustup toolchain uninstall'), rust-docs (each toolchain's installed rust-docs component, removed with 'rustup component remove rust-docs'), claude-transcripts (Claude Code sessions untouched for 'idleDays', always to the Trash and never pre-selected). See docs/DESIGN.md.

categories.name: Xcode derived data & device support
categories.desc: Xcode build cache, device-support & documentation cache — rebuilt on next build.

categories.name: Clang module cache
categories.desc: Precompiled modules clang & swiftc keep for builds outside Xcode's DerivedData (command-line, SwiftPM, CMake) in your user cache folder — rebuilt by the next build.

categories.name: Xcode archives
categories.desc: Release .xcarchive bundles — hold the dSYMs needed to symbolicate crash reports from shipped builds. Do NOT clear if you still support those releases.

categories.name: Go build & tooling cache
categories.desc: go build/test cache, gopls/goimports indexes & golangci-lint cache — regenerated on build.

categories.name: Go module cache
categories.desc: Downloaded Go modules ($GOPATH/pkg/mod) — re-fetched on next 'go build'.

categories.name: Node / npm cache
categories.desc: npm download cache, npx package cache, logs, prebuilt binaries & Node's compile cache — re-fetched on install or rebuilt on the next run.

categories.name: JS build-tool caches
categories.desc: Turbo/Vite/webpack/Parcel/ESLint/Prettier & Electron download caches — rebuilt on next build.

categories.name: pnpm store
categories.desc: pnpm's content-addressable package store — re-downloaded on next install.

categories.name: Yarn cache
categories.desc: Yarn's global package cache — re-downloaded on next install.

categories.name: Gradle user cache
categories.desc: Gradle downloaded dependencies, wrapper distributions, build cache & daemon state in ~/.gradle — re-fetched on build. Stop the Gradle daemon first if one is running.

categories.name: Maven repository
categories.desc: Locally cached Maven artifacts (~/.m2) — re-downloaded on next build.

categories.name: sbt / Ivy caches
categories.desc: sbt launchers & Ivy dependency cache — re-fetched on next build.

categories.name: Cargo registry cache
categories.desc: Cargo's downloaded crate cache, git checkouts & rustup downloads — re-fetched on next build.

categories.name: Rust toolchain
categories.desc: An installed toolchain that is neither your default nor stable (GBs each) — removed with 'rustup toolchain uninstall'; rustup downloads it again if a project asks for it.

categories.name: Rust offline docs
categories.desc: The rust-docs component of each toolchain (~0.9 GB apiece) that 'rustup doc' opens offline — removed with 'rustup component remove rust-docs'; 'rustup component add rust-docs' brings it back.

categories.name: sccache compile cache
categories.desc: sccache's shared Rust/C compilation cache — rebuilt on next build. Project target/ dirs are offered per repo by the project scan.

categories.name: Python cache (pip / uv / poetry)
categories.desc: pip, uv, poetry & pyenv download caches plus ruff/mypy indexes — re-downloaded or rebuilt on next run.

categories.name: ML model & training caches
categories.desc: Hugging Face / PyTorch / TensorFlow / Keras model downloads & W&B run cache — regenerable, but often many GB to re-download.

categories.name: Conda package cache
categories.desc: Downloaded conda packages & tarballs — re-downloaded on next install. Your environments themselves are untouched.

categories.name: Ruby / Bundler caches
categories.desc: rbenv build cache, gem specs & Bundler package cache — re-fetched on next 'bundle install'.

categories.name: Bun cache
categories.desc: Bun's install cache — re-downloaded on next install.

categories.name: Deno cache
categories.desc: Deno's module & compilation cache — re-fetched on next run.

categories.name: CocoaPods cache
categories.desc: CocoaPods spec & pod download cache — re-fetched on next 'pod install'.

categories.name: Swift Package Manager cache
categories.desc: SwiftPM's cloned-dependency & artifact cache — re-fetched on next resolve.

categories.name: Docker buildx cache
categories.desc: buildx build cache on the host (not the daemon's data) — rebuilt on next build. Docker credentials in ~/.docker are untouched.

categories.name: Cloud CLI caches & logs
categories.desc: kubectl / AWS / gcloud / Azure / wrangler CLI caches & logs — regenerated on next command. Credentials and configs are untouched.

categories.name: PHP Composer cache
categories.desc: Composer's package download cache — re-fetched on next install.

categories.name: NuGet package cache
categories.desc: Locally cached .NET NuGet packages — re-downloaded on next restore.

categories.name: Bazel / Zig / OCaml caches
categories.desc: Bazel & Zig build caches and opam's download cache — rebuilt or re-fetched on next build.

categories.name: Dart / Flutter caches
categories.desc: Flutter engine cache & the Dart pub package cache — re-downloaded on next 'pub get' / build.

categories.name: AI CLI tool caches
categories.desc: Scratch caches for terminal AI tools — regenerated on next run. Sessions, settings & credentials (~/.claude, ~/.codex) are not part of this row.

categories.name: Claude Code transcripts older than 30 days
categories.desc: Sessions untouched for 30+ days — each transcript with its subagent & tool-output folder — moved to the Trash. A trashed session cannot be resumed or reopened (in Claude Desktop too) until you put it back. Running sessions, auto memory & settings are never touched. To stop them piling up, set desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays in ~/.claude/settings.json.

categories.name: CI runner caches
categories.desc: Local GitLab/CircleCI runner & SonarQube analysis caches — re-fetched on next run.

categories.name: Shell & CLI tool residue
categories.desc: zsh completion dumps, oh-my-zsh cache and curl/wget scratch state — regenerated on next shell start or download.

categories.name: pre-commit hook cache
categories.desc: pre-commit's installed hook environments — rebuilt on next run.

categories.name: mise / asdf tool cache
categories.desc: mise's download cache — re-fetched on next install. Installed tool versions are untouched.

categories.name: JetBrains caches & logs
categories.desc: IntelliJ/PyCharm/etc. index caches & logs — rebuilt on next launch.

categories.name: Zed language servers & logs
categories.desc: Language servers, Node.js & Prettier that Zed downloads on demand, plus its logs & hang traces — fetched again when a file needs them. Settings, extensions & agent threads are kept.

categories.name: Playwright / Puppeteer browsers
categories.desc: Downloaded test browsers — re-installed by 'playwright install'.

categories.name: Homebrew download cache
categories.desc: Downloaded bottles & installers ('brew cleanup') — re-fetched on demand.

categories.name: PlatformIO download cache
categories.desc: Downloaded package archives & registry cache ('pio system prune --cache'), and the archives ESP32 tools were unpacked from — re-fetched on demand. Installed platforms & toolchains are their own unchecked row.

categories.name: PlatformIO platforms & toolchains
categories.desc: Installed dev platforms, toolchains & frameworks (GBs) — the next 'pio run' downloads what its project needs again (network needed). PlatformIO itself (~/.platformio/penv) and its settings stay.

categories.name: Android build caches
categories.desc: Android SDK/Gradle & Android Studio transient caches, logs and interrupted SDK downloads — rebuilt by the toolchain.

categories.name: Android emulator snapshots
categories.desc: Quick-boot snapshots of your AVDs — the next launch cold-boots and saves a fresh one. Apps & data installed in the AVD are kept.

categories.name: Unused Android system images
categories.desc: Emulator OS images (GBs each) that NO AVD on this Mac boots from — an image an AVD uses is never in this row. Re-install from Android Studio's SDK Manager or 'sdkmanager' if you create an AVD with one later.

categories.name: Idle AVD image
categories.desc: Every AVD that boots this emulator image has gone 60+ days without running. Deleting it keeps their apps & data, but they will not boot until it is reinstalled from Android Studio's SDK Manager.

categories.name: Android NDK, CMake & SDK sources
categories.desc: C/C++ toolchains (NDK, CMake — GBs) and the framework sources the IDE shows — a Java/Kotlin-only build needs none of them. Gradle (AGP 4.2+) installs an NDK or CMake again when a build needs one; or reinstall from Android Studio's SDK Manager.

categories.name: Older Android build-tools & platforms
categories.desc: Every SDK build-tools and platform version except the newest of each — a project that targets an older one has Gradle or Android Studio download it again on its next build.

categories.name: Expo caches
categories.desc: Expo's downloaded client/template/schema caches — re-fetched on demand. Your Expo login (~/.expo/state.json) is untouched.
